title: Dilution-to-Extinction DNA Extraction
author: Shelby J Barnes
materials: The following is used with BD Accuri C6 Plus Software for the BD Accuri C6 Plus Flow Cytometer systems from BD Biosciences (San Jose, California, United States).

All culturing hardware (carboys, flasks, glassware, PTFE plates, sealing mats, stir bars) are washed first with dishwasher or lab-grade detergent; rinsed with hot tap water, cold tap water, and then DI water; and let dry.

Once DNA is extracted, prepare the PCR master mix for the number of samples Volume of gDNA will vary depending on concentration. Can use taq Polymerase kit (Invitrogen, OneTaq, etc) and dNTP's or premade master mix (GoTaq G2, etc).

steps.title: Prepare Sample Collection Vessels
steps.instruction: Prepare sterile, acid-washed carboys for sample collection.

substeps.instruction: Soak carboys in a 10% HCl acid bath overnight.
Rinse six times with DI water and MilliQ water.
Apply lids or wrap in foil and autoclave prior to storage or use.

steps.title: Collect and Filter Samples
steps.instruction: Collect samples from the source of interest and perform initial filtration.

substeps.instruction: Collect samples using the prepared carboys, wearing gloves and taking precautions to avoid contamination.
Transport samples to the laboratory with the shortest delay possible.
Filter samples using a 2.7µm Whatman GF/D glass fiber filter to exclude large aggregates/particles.

steps.title: Enumerate DTE Inoculum Sample
steps.instruction: Determine the total cell concentration of the inoculum to ensure it is between 1,000 and 5*10^6 cells/µL for BDAccuri counting range.

substeps.instruction: If samples are higher than 5*10^6 cells/µL, make appropriate dilutions in sterile medium.
Transfer 400 µL of desired controls (stained/unstained medium and stained/unstained E. coli) into 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 198 µL of each control to a 96-well plate.
Stain samples and one control with SYBR Green to a 1x final concentration (add 2 µL 100x SYBR Green to 198 µL sample).
Incubate samples for 30 minutes in the dark.
Transfer 198 µL of each sample, in triplicate, into a round-bottom 96-well plate.
Add two artificial medium controls (one stained, one unstained) to the plate.

steps.title: Configure Flow Cytometer and Count Cells
steps.instruction: Set up the BDAccuri and calculate cell concentration using gated regions.

substeps.instruction: Set general run settings: 'Run with Limits', volume 10µL, flow rate medium, Thresholds (FSC/SSC: 10, FL1/FITC: 100).
Adjust thresholds using the manual collect tab with unstained controls to exclude noise.
Use plots (FSC vs green fluorescence, SSC vs green fluorescence, and green fluorescence vs yellow fluorescence) to evaluate counts.
Apply a global gate using stained artificial medium to exclude medium signal, customizing the gate for individual samples/isolates as needed.
Set SIP settings: SIP Rinse 1 cycle per sample and SIP Clean after completed run.

steps.title: Inoculate Deep 96-Well Plates
steps.instruction: Dilute cells in medium and distribute into plates to achieve an average of 1–3 cells per well.

substeps.instruction: Prepare artificial medium according to SJB Artificial Media Protocol or medium of choice.
Calculate inoculation volume (e.g., for 900mL final volume, 5*10^3 cells/mL inoculum, and 1-3 cells/1.7mL final concentration, use ~106 µL inoculum).
Swirl inoculated medium thoroughly and aliquot into a sterile liquid reservoir.
Distribute 1.7 mL per well into sterile, acid-washed 2.1 mL PTFE deep 96-well plates using a P100-1200 µL multichannel pipette or Eppendorf epMotion 5075.
Seal plates with sterile silicon lids.
Incubate plates at room temperature (~25°C) for 2 - 4 weeks.

steps.title: Identify and Scale Up Positive Wells
steps.instruction: Identify positive wells and transfer them to larger flasks for growth.

substeps.instruction: Verify negative controls (four corners of the plate); they should have a cell density of 10^3 or less. If a biotic signature is present, discard the plate.
Identify positive wells (cell densities of 10^4 and higher).
Transfer 200 µL of each positive well to a 250 mL flask containing 50 mL of the chosen medium.

steps.title: Culture Growth and Filtration
steps.instruction: Monitor growth and filter cells at the late log phase.

substeps.instruction: Count newly transferred cultures following the enumeration section.
Take daily cell counts and plot growth curves.
When cultures reach late log phase, create a new transfer group (200 µL culture into 50 mL fresh medium).
Filter 40-45 mL of late log phase culture using a 0.1-0.2 µm Supor PES filter (via hand or vacuum filtration).
Store filters with cells at -20°C.

steps.title: Extract and Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from filtered cells and quantify the yield.

substeps.instruction: Extract DNA using the GenElute™ Bacterial Genomic DNA Kit.
Quantify gDNA concentration using a Qubit Fluorometer.
Prepare PCR tubes with: 15 µL Master Mix, 3 µL gDNA, and 32 µL H2O.

Run thermocycler with Lid Temp 105°C and Sample Volume 50 µL using these steps: 1) 94°C for 3:00 mins; 2) 94°C for 0:30 mins; 3) 50.8°C for 0:30 mins; 4) 72°C for 2:00 mins; 5) Repeat steps 2-4 for 34x; 6) 72°C for 10:00 mins; 7) 4°C infinite hold.
Store PCR products at 4°C or proceed to gel/purification.

steps.title: Verify PCR via Agarose Gel
steps.instruction: Run a 1.5% agarose gel to verify the correct band length (usually 1500 bp).

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 50 mL solution of 1.5% agarose and 1x TAE Buffer; microwave in 30-second intervals until dissolved.
Add 30 µL of 100x SYBR Green to the molten agarose, swirl, and pour into a gel mold.
Remove bubbles and let the gel harden in a dark place for at least one hour.

steps.title: Purify and Quantify PCR Product
steps.instruction: Purify the amplified DNA and determine concentration.

substeps.instruction: Purify PCR product using either the GeneJet PCR purification kit or Ampure XP beads.
Quantify purified PCR product using a Qubit assay.

steps.title: Prepare Sequencing Samples
steps.instruction: Set up samples for 16S rRNA sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Create two sequencing samples per PCR product: one for 16S rRNA 27F Forward and one for 1492R Reverse.
For each sample (Total volume 15 µL), combine: 5 µL of 10 µM primer (27F or 1492R), ~40 ng of DNA in 10 µL of PCR product, and Molecular H2O to reach the final volume.
Submit sequencing requests to Azenta (Genewiz) or another facility.
